channel.title: TDEE Check blog
channel.description: Practical guides on TDEE, calories, macros and weight management, reviewed by a dietitian.

item.title: How to Calculate Your TDEE: A Step by Step Guide
item.description: Learn the TDEE formula step by step, with a worked example, the activity multiplier table and the mistakes that make results come out wrong.

item.title: TDEE vs BMR: What Is the Difference and Which Do You Need?
item.description: BMR is the calories you burn at rest, TDEE is everything you burn in a day. How the two numbers connect, a worked example with both, and which one sets your calorie target.

item.title: How Accurate Are TDEE Calculators? (And How to Fix Your Number)
item.description: TDEE calculators land within about 10 percent for most people, but activity guesses can push the error higher. Where the error hides and the 2 to 3 week test that fixes your number.

item.title: What Is a Calorie Deficit? Sizes, Safety and a Worked Example
item.description: A calorie deficit means eating fewer calories than you burn. The four deficit sizes compared, the 3,500 kcal rule explained honestly, safety floors, and how to build yours step by step.

item.title: What Is a Good TDEE? Average TDEE by Age, Sex and Activity
item.description: There is no single good TDEE. Typical ranges by sex and activity level, how age lowers your number through muscle loss, and how to find your own tested maintenance figure.

item.title: How to Use TDEE for Weight Loss: The Safe Deficit Guide
item.description: Use your TDEE to lose weight safely: find maintenance, pick a 250 to 500 kcal deficit, set protein at 0.7 to 1 gram per pound, track for 2 to 3 weeks, and adjust at each plateau.

item.title: Why Your TDEE Changed: 7 Reasons Your Number Moves
item.description: Your TDEE follows your body and your life. Weight change, muscle gain or loss, drifting steps, aging, adaptive thermogenesis, sleep and water weight explained, with what to do about each.

item.title: TDEE for Beginners: The Complete Plain-Language Guide
item.description: TDEE explained with zero jargon: the four ways your body spends energy, BMR in plain words, the activity multiplier, a tiny glossary, and three things to do in your first week.

item.title: Eating Below Your BMR: Is It Safe?
item.description: Your BMR funds your brain, heart and organs before you move at all. Why eating below it chronically backfires, the supervised exception, who must never do it, and the safer deficit method.

item.title: How Activity Levels Really Work (and Why Most People Overestimate)
item.description: The five activity multipliers translated into real jobs and step counts, why a desk job plus gym is usually light or moderate, a step based self-test, and the 259 kcal cost of one level too high.

item.title: Reverse Dieting Explained: Raising Calories After a Diet
item.description: After a diet, climb back to maintenance in weekly steps of 50 to 150 kcal. Who it suits, the honest mechanism behind it, the early water weight rise, and when to skip it and eat at maintenance.
